title: Sharp MZ, Thomson, DAAD/DOS and Apple Lisa discovery
summary: Review thirteen queue/search candidates; promote nine projects and close three old discovery tasks
notes: CPU queue returned zero unresolved source/target areas, so no CPU value was inferred merely to satisfy a quota. Fresh GitHub repository/README searches were: '"Sharp MZ" disassembly source reconstruction', '"Thomson MO5" source homebrew tooling', '"Enterprise 128" source port Z80', '"Apple Lisa" assembly source utility', then broadened to 'Sharp MZ source', 'Thomson MO5 emulator', 'Enterprise 128 homebrew', and 'Apple Lisa utility'. Reviewed/promoted: lukq/mz-basictoqd, bver/arem-mzf-parser, Zlika/theodore, qam4/crayon, d235j/lisa-utilities, GyroPilot/Apple-LisaFileMover, Utodev/DRC, lab313ru/dsbxida and stepleton/NeoWidEx. Known results michalhucik/mz800emu and kpouer/Maurice were duplicates of indexed projects; the Enterprise searches returned no promotable candidate. NeoWidEx supersedes its 2026-10-10 deferred review without erasing that historical decision. Pobtastic 180 was re-audited after upstream activity. Read-only review: no upstream code, compiler, emulator, ROM, image, device or destructive utility was run.

project.title: BASIC to QD — Sharp MZ BASIC transfer and listing tools
project.display_title: BASIC to QD — Sharp MZ BASIC transfer and listing tools
source_language: Sharp MZ BASIC text and binary files
project.status: Browser transfer/listing utility documented upstream; not independently executed

identity.narrative: The repository documents a browser application that turns Sharp MZ-800 BASIC text into Quick Disk or cassette data and includes a reverse listing utility for MZF BASIC files.

classification.narrative: This is original retro-development and transfer tooling, not a reverse-engineered program or RE-derived port.

source_cpu.narrative: Source CPU is not applicable: the tool transforms BASIC text and binary media records rather than analysing an original machine-code program.

target_cpu.narrative: Target CPU is not applicable: the outputs are BASIC/media data, not native machine code.

build.narrative: The README gives an end-to-end browser workflow and names supported BASIC versions and emulators; the application was not executed in this review.
build.limitations: Primary documentation review only; no generated image was loaded into an emulator.

runtime_profiles.narrative: No minimum browser, host CPU, RAM, or physical Sharp MZ hardware requirement is stated.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the reviewed primary documentation; this does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The README names EmuZ-800/mz800emu usage and separate Quick Disk and cassette output paths; this entry tracks the converter/listing tool rather than those emulators.

build.limitations: Static source review only; Ruby dependencies and parser execution were not run.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The documented Ruby/Bundler/BinData host requirement is captured, with no minimum CPU or RAM inferred.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the README or inspected parser; this does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The input is the AREM assembler-source container used on Sharp MZ-800; the project is distinct from general MZF disk/tape emulators.

project.title: DoSBoXIDA — DOSBox-X–based IDA debugger
project.status: DOSBox-X fork with independent IDA debugger plugin; not independently built

identity.narrative: DoSBoXIDA is a DOSBox-X-based project that connects MS-DOS program execution to IDA debugging.

classification.narrative: Although it is a fork, the inspected dsbxida plugin implements its own IDA debugger integration and DOSBox callback handling, so it is a distinct archaeology tool rather than an ordinary mirror.

source_cpu.narrative: The README identifies MS-DOS programs and the plugin accepts DOS executable contexts through IDA's PC processor/debugger interfaces, supporting x86 source-program metadata.

target_cpu.narrative: No native host/output CPU requirement was found; DOSBox-X lineage and IDA support do not establish a host architecture.

build.narrative: The repository includes plugin and Visual Studio integration, but the README does not provide a complete reproducible build procedure and no build was run.
build.limitations: Static source review only; no IDA installation, plugin build, DOS program or emulator process was run.

runtime_profiles.narrative: No minimum IDA, host OS, CPU or RAM requirement was established from the inspected primary files.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the reviewed primary documentation or plugin source; this does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The older idados_dosbox README names dsbxida as its successor; dsbxida is based on DOSBox-X and carries the current independent plugin implementation.

identity.narrative: NeoWidEx is a low-level formatting and diagnostic utility for Apple's 10 MB Widget hard drive on Lisa 2 systems.

classification.narrative: It is substantial original homebrew and hardware-development software, not a reverse-engineered application or RE-derived port.

source_cpu.narrative: Source CPU is not applicable because NeoWidEx is original software rather than analysis of a pre-existing binary.

target_cpu.narrative: The repository explicitly describes roughly 10,000 lines of 68000 macro assembly and a native Lisa boot image, supporting Motorola 68000 target metadata.

build.narrative: BUILDING documents EASy68K assembly, srec_cat conversion at address $800 and bootable DC42 generation with the Stepleton bootloader; no step was executed here.
build.limitations: Read-only documentation review; destructive drive operations, assembly, boot image generation and hardware/emulator execution were not performed.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The README's ROM, floppy/emulator and Widget access requirements are captured exactly; no CPU or RAM minimum is inferred.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the reviewed README/build documentation; this does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The README distinguishes NeoWidEx from Apple's Widex and credits related BLU/UsbWidEx work without claiming shared source.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the reviewed primary files; this does not establish non-use.
